description: Fixed kinematics of the point worm's locomotor primitives. Every value is from published off-food data; 'verified' means read in the text, 'figure' means read from a figure by eye (about +/-10%).

v_max_mm_per_s.source: Zhao et al. 2003 J Neurosci 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.23-12-05319.2003, Fig 3A: 184 um/s at the start of off-food locomotion; Ben Arous et al. 2009 PLoS One 10.1371/journal.pone.0007584, Fig 2E: about 0.17 mm/s without food. Equal to the crawl speed the step duration derives from.

omega_max_deg_per_s.source: Pierce-Shimomura et al. 1999 J Neurosci 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.19-21-09557.1999, Results: a turning rate above 50 deg/s defines a sharp turn, so a run turns below it.

reversal_speed_mm_per_s.source: Zhao et al. 2003, Fig 5A: mean reversal speed 140 um/s.

reversal_duration_s.source: Zhao et al. 2003, Fig 5B: 2.3 +/- 1.6 s for reversals without a following omega (n = 249) and 3.4 +/- 1.8 s with one (n = 135), pooled by count (mean and SD of the mixture).

omega_angle_deg.source: Broekmans et al. 2016 eLife 10.7554/eLife.17227, Fig 4C: foraging omega turns reorient ventrally, mostly 100-200 deg, peak near 150-160 deg.

omega_duration_s.source: Broekmans et al. 2016, Fig 4-figure supplement 1: escape omega turns 7 +/- 3 s; foraging omega duration is not reported.

delta_angle_deg.source: Broekmans et al. 2016, Fig 4C: delta turns over-turn through the ventral side to reorient dorsally, about 30-170 deg, peak near 80-100 deg.

delta_duration_s.source: Broekmans et al. 2016, Fig 4-figure supplement 1: delta turns 6 +/- 2 s (N = 348).

hazard_range_per_s.source: Gray et al. 2005 PNAS 10.1073/pnas.0409009101, Fig 1E: short reversals, long reversals and omegas range from about 0.05 to 3 per minute (0.0008-0.05 per second) across on-food, early off-food and dispersal conditions; the range spans them with margin.
